title: Rabbi Chama bar Ukva
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was the student of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina, as Hyman notes that we always find Rav Chama bar Ukva transmitting in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina, as in [Pesachim 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.52b.3) and [Sukkah 37b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.37b.10); Hyman proposes this reading in [Kiddushin 55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.55a.7) and 72a; Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 9:1; Terumot 3:3; Kilayim 8:2; Pesachim 7:8; and Taanit 3:6. In [Yerushalmi Megillah 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.2.4.6): “Rabbi Chelbo, Rav Chama bar Guria in the name of Rav Chama bar Ukva in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina”; Hyman proposes “Rabbi Chelbo in the name of Rav Chama bar Guria, and Rav Chama bar Ukva in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina.”
Likewise he spoke in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as in Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 2:1;
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, as in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 7, end of halakhah 2.

Hyman infers that he was friendly with Rabbi Zeira, as implied in [Yevamot 71a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.71a.15): “Rabbi Chama bar Ukva asked; Rabbi Zeira said: Come and hear.” And with Rabbi Levi, as at the end of Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 42: Rabbi Chama bar Ukva and the Rabbis were sitting and wondering why Scripture traced the generations of Ishmael; Rabbi Levi passed by; they said: “Here is the master of the teaching; let us ask him.” Abaye cites Rabbi Chama bar Ukva in [Kiddushin 72a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.72a.4).
Rabbi Yonah said that Rabbi Chama bar Akiva (Hyman proposes Ukva) said, as in [Yerushalmi Eruvin 3:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.3.7.3).
Rabbi Yose raised a difficulty against him: Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah, beginning of chapter 1.
Rabbi Yirmeyah in his name: Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 7:1.
He is likewise mentioned in [Pesachim 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.82a.2), saying: “It is not difficult: here,” etc.[^3]

notes.text: רחב״ג is Rav Chama bar Guria by the full spelling immediately before it, not Rabbi Chama. Hyman’s correction separates two chains rather than assigning Chama bar Guria a new teacher. All chapter/halakhah locations are Jerusalem Talmud; Akiva/Ukva and Rav/Rabbi title variants remain.

Pesachim 52b directly names Chama bar Ukva reporting Yose son of Chanina. Hyman’s always assertion, separation of the Megillah chains, Akiva-to-Ukva emendation and inference of friendship remain his; one attestation is not exhaustive proof.

Pesachim and Sukkah name Ukva and Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina. Kiddushin 55a has Chama son of Rabbi Akiva, while 72a has Abaye transmitting from Chama bar Ukva through Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina. Heilprin proposes Ukva at 55a as well. Yerushalmi Megillah prints Guria, Ukva and Yose in sequence. Hyman proposes dividing that sequence into two chains. Yerushalmi Eruvin retains bar Akiva, which Hyman proposes to change to bar Ukva. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1355&lang=en).
